headline: Connecticut lowers flags for DOT worker killed on I-95 as memorial services begin
dek: State flags are at half-staff Friday for Elvin Hernandez, a CTDOT employee killed while working on Interstate 95 in Fairfield, as his family and colleagues gather for memorial services.
body: Connecticut state and U.S. flags are being flown at half-staff from sunrise to sunset Friday, Oct. 2, as the state honors Elvin Hernandez, a Connecticut Department of Transportation employee killed while working on Interstate 95 in Fairfield. Gov. Ned Lamont's Oct. 1 directive applies to the State Capitol and other state-operated buildings, grounds and facilities. The governor's office is also encouraging municipalities, schools, businesses and residents to lower their flags for the day (https://portal.ct.gov/governor/news/press-releases/2026/10-2026/governor-lamont-directs-flags-to-half-staff-friday-in-honor-of-elvin-hernandez).

The timing is tied to memorial and interment services scheduled Friday in Bridgeport and Easton. WFSB reported that Hernandez's viewing is planned in Bridgeport from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., followed by burial at Mount Grove Easton Cemetery. Those arrangements give the state observance a specific local focus: a public tribute in government buildings is taking place alongside services for Hernandez's family, friends and CTDOT colleagues (https://www.wfsb.com/2026/09/30/funeral-arrangements-set-dot-worker-killed-i-95-fairfield/).

Hernandez was 60 and worked for CTDOT from 2010 until his death. The agency said he was based at its Stratford garage. Its initial Sept. 25 statement said he was doing road maintenance on I-95 in Fairfield when he was struck by a motor vehicle. Lamont, Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz and Transportation Commissioner Garrett Eucalitto described the death as a loss for a public employee whose job put him alongside moving traffic (https://portal.ct.gov/dot/ctdot-press-releases/2026/ctdot-mourns-the-death-of-ctdot-employee-elvin-hernandez?language=en_US).

The crash happened near Exit 20, according to Connecticut State Police information reported by the Connecticut Post. Hernandez had gotten out of a CTDOT dump truck to remove debris when a 2006 Buick Lucerne entered the right shoulder and struck him. Police said lifesaving efforts were attempted and Hernandez was taken to Bridgeport Hospital, where he died from his injuries. The interstate's southbound lanes were closed for several hours during the investigation (https://www.ctpost.com/news/article/fairfield-i95-dot-worker-elvin-hernandez-death-22452420.php).

The driver, identified in the Connecticut Post report as Edward Myers of Derby, faces allegations rather than a finding of guilt. The report said Myers was charged with second-degree manslaughter with a motor vehicle, operating under the influence, driving without an ignition interlock device, failure to maintain a proper lane and possession of a controlled substance. A judge set bond at $2 million, according to that report. The charges remain allegations, and the criminal case can produce additional court findings that were not available in the sources reviewed for this update.

The case has also renewed attention to Connecticut's work-zone and roadside-safety rules. CTDOT officials are urging drivers to slow down, move over, put away phones and never drive under the influence near highway crews or first responders. The department said it has about 3,300 employees; its statement presented Hernandez's death as the kind of danger highway workers face when traffic passes close to an active work area. That warning is broader than this single crash: every roadside crew depends on approaching drivers recognizing the work zone early and changing speed and position before reaching it.

Friday's half-staff order is therefore both a memorial and a safety reminder. The state has confirmed the observance and the service schedule, but the legal process surrounding the crash is still pending. NorthEast News will treat any future court development as a separate update rather than implying that the allegations against Myers have been resolved. For now, the confirmed next steps are Hernandez's Bridgeport viewing, his Easton burial and the statewide flag observance during the hours set by the governor.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Connecticut honors DOT worker Elvin Hernandez
seoDescription: Connecticut lowers flags for CTDOT employee Elvin Hernandez as memorial services follow his death on I-95 in Fairfield.
